newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on Egypt, short covering.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on Egypt, short covering.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on commercial buying, short covering and on news Egypt over the weekend bought 200,000 tonnes of U.S. soft red winter wheat, traders said.
The commercial buying centered on Cargill Inc's purchase of 3.5 million bushels of July and Continental Grain was a noted purchaser of 1.5 million bushels of July, traders said.
The short covering was tied to signals the market was oversold for the short term with the July nine-day relative strength (RSI) index early nearing the 30 percent mark.
An RSI of 30 or less is indicative of an oversold market and an RSI of 70 or more is evidence of an overbought market.
The May was firm as shorts got out of that month before its expiration at 1201 CDT Tuesday. Traders expected an orderly and quiet expiration of the May contract.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed one to six cents per bushel higher, with July up six at $3.94-3/4 a bushel.
The market was under pressure much of the day from rainfall over the weekend in some key wheat areas.
Showers were reported over the weekend in portions of the Kansas wheat growing area and also in portions of Oklahoma and Texas.
But northwest Kansas remained generally dry and more rain was needed to ensure satisfactory production in that key area of the state, grain dealers said.
Refco Inc was the key seller of five million bushels of July, traders said.

Little direction came from USDA's weekly export inspections report released early Monday. USDA said U.S. wheat inspected for export during the week ended May 15 totaled 9.282 million bushels, within the range of expectations for eight million to 14.0 million bushels.
E.D. and F. Man International bought 1.5 million bushels of July, SAK Futures bought one million July and Smith Barney bought one million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 16,000 contracts, above the 14,925 traded Friday.

In wheat options, FIMAT bought 2,200 Sept $4.10 puts at 33 cents and sold 2,200 Sept $3.90 puts at 21 cents, traders said. Prudential Securities sold 150 September $3.80 puts at 15 to 16 cents and Paine Webber sold 100 July $4.00 Puts at 21-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,000 contracts, above the 6,571 traded Friday.
